Predictions for Future Honest Trailers

*   _Godzilla (1998)_: To coincide with the release of _Godzilla (2014)_.  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _A New Hope_: When _The Force Awakens_ is released.  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _Transformers: Revenge of The Fallen_ and _Transformers: Dark of the Moon_: The first when _Age of Extinction_ comes out, the second when _The Last Knight_ came out, followed by a trailer for the Roast of Optimus Prime.  
    *    For the _Bumblebee_ spinoff, _The Transformers: The Movie_  
        *    Confirmed. But not for leading up to _Bumblebee_, but rather in the lead up to _Transformers: Rise of the Beasts_.

    *   _Revenge of the Fallen_ is confirmed.  
    *    And eventually, _Bumblebee_ (a.k.a. _Bee Movie_)

*   _The Lone Ranger (2013)_  
*   _Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D._  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _Power Rangers RPM_  
    *   _Power Rangers Beast Morphers_ (aka _Power Rangers Venjisys_)

*   _Big Hero 6_. "Starring: Tony Stark Jr. (Hiro), Black Logan (Wasabi), Mexican Rapunzel (Honey Lemon), Not-Zilla (Fred), Miss America (GoGo Tomago), AND The Stay-Puff Marshmallow Man (Baymax)!"  
    *    Confirmed. Hiro is even called a "miniature version of Tony Stark."

*    Something from Pixar. Most likely one of the _Toy Story_ or _Cars_ movies.  
    *    Confirmed, they covered _Toy Story 1_.

*   _Tomorrowland_  
    *    "Starring: Teenage Jennifer Lawrence (Casey), Robert Downey III (Frank), Full House (Nix), Robo-Gadgets (the evil robots)..."

*   _Mad Max_: We've waited too long for this one, let's be honest.  
    *    Confirmed for _Fury Road_. The original trilogy came later.
Advertisement:

*   _Inside Out_  
    *    Starring: The Kid Whose Last Name The Fandom Got Wrong For Months (Riley Andersen), Happy Happy Joy Joy (Joy), The Lady From The Office (Sadness), Red Lewis Black (Anger), Taffyta Muttonfudge (Disgust), Flint Lockwood (Fear), and A _Foster's Home for Imaginary Friends_ resident (Bing Bong).  
    *    Confirmed. They even called Bing Bong "Foster's Head for Imaginary Friends".

*   _Fantastic Four (2015)_  
    *    Starring: Not Quite My Tempo (Mr. Fantastic), Rooney'sSister (Invisible Woman), The OtherMichael Jordan (Human Torch), Hot Rocks (The Thing), DiscountMorgan Freeman (Dr. Storm), Samuel Sterns (Dr. Allen), Homer Simpson (the teacher), Half of Tim & Eric (Reed's stepfather) and Doom on You for Watching This Movie (Dr. Doom).  
    *    Confirmed, _Whiplash_ reference and all.

*   _Point Break (1991)_: To coincide with the release of _Point Break (2015)_. Expect many Take Thats aimed at the latter.  
    *    Confirmed. It didn't coincide with the release of the 2015 film, but instead two years later, but it did have a Take That! at the 2015 film.

*   _Daredevil (2015)_: To coincide with the release of _Jessica Jones (2015)_.  
    *   Jossed.

*    One of the '70s Peanuts movies, such as _Race for Your Life, Charlie Brown_: To coincide with _The Peanuts Movie_.  
    *   Jossed.

*   _Zootopia (2016)_. The trailer will be totally packed with Furry Fandom jokes.  
    *    "Starring: What Does the Fox Say? (Nick), Slip Me A Poison Apple (Judy), the Author of the Journals, My Brother (Mayor Lionheart), Sexy Sadie (Gazelle), The Mayor's Gonna Have My ASS!!! (Chief Bogo), Cheasel T. Weasel Ripoff (Duke Weaselton), the Brain, Minus Pinky (Mr. Big), Fox News (the newscasters) and Internet Explorer (the sloths)"  
    *    Confirmed, furry jokes and all.
Advertisement:
*   _The Incredible Hulk (2008)_: For a future Marvel Cinematic Universe movie or the tenth anniversary of the MCU.  
    *    Starring: NotMark Ruffalo (Edward Norton), Arwen (Liv Tyler), Doomsday (Abomination)...  
    *    Confirmed for _Avengers: Infinity War_ (which is the tenth anniversary of the MCU).

*   _The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water_  
    *    Starring: Square Minion (SpongeBob), The Pink Fatty (Patrick), Eeyore (Squidward), Creepy Girl In a Squirrel Costume (Sandy), Scrooge MacKrab (Mr. Krabs), PlinkPlank (Plankton), I'm the Daddy Now!!! (Bubbles the Dolphin), and Scrappy Doo Times 6 (the talking seagulls).  
    *    Or the first one, _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_.

*   _Spirited Away_  
*   _Superman Returns_  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _Thomas and the Magic Railroad_  
    *    Starring: The Little Engine That Could (Thomas), ConDoctor Who (Mr. Conductor), Peter Fonda? What are you doing here? (Burnett Stone), Matilda (Lily), Buzz and Delete (Splatter and Dodge), Vin Diesel the 10th (Diesel 10), The Claw (Pinchy), Chuggington (Percy), Frenchy Jones (Stacy Jones), Not Another Teen Movie (Patch), The Sodor Express (Gordon), The Red and the Furious (James), The Tram-Pariah (Toby), Forest Whitaker (Henry), The Kardashians (Annie and Clarabel), The Magic Cameo Bus (Bertie), Get to the Chopper (Harold), Indiana Groans (Billy), The Random Baaalll (Tumbleweed), and Fun Size (2012) (Junior). And... Not Starring All These Characters from the Show: Edward, Terrence, Duck, Oliver, 'Arry and Bert, Diesel, The Diesel, Derek the Diesel, Daisy, Bulgy, Bulstrode, George the Steamroller, Stepney, Cranky the Crane, Toad, SC Ruffey, Donald and Douglas, Bill and Ben, BoCo, Old Slow Coach, Mavis, Tiger Moth, The Narrow Gauge Railway, and PT Boomer.

    *   _Superman_ (1978) and _Batman (1989)_ confirmed.  
    *    Alternatively, _Batman Returns_ for _Ant-Man and the Wasp_ due to the presence of Michelle Pfeiffer.  
        *   _Batman: The Animated Series_, _Batman Returns_ and _Batman Forever_ confirmed.

*   _Groundhog Day_: Since February 2 (Groundhog Day) in 2016 is on a Tuesday, when the trailers come out.  
    *   Jossed

*   _Descendants_: If so, then it might be the first Made-for-TV Movie covered by Honest Trailers (if they don't do _Duel_ first).  
    *    If they do _Descendants_, it should be for Descendants 2.

    *    Starring: Prince Mad Love (Ben) Goth Liv (Mal), The Prince of Thieves (Jay), Sofia (Evie), American Beast (Carlos), **NOT**Angelina Jolie (Maleficient), Equestria Girl (Audrey), The human dwarf (Doug), The Stepson (Chad), Jane Arc (Jane), Genki Girl (Lonnie), Ms. Red Robin (Fairy Godmother), Abis Mal (Jafar), and Aaron Stone Lives! (Aaron Stone Video Game).

*   _Deadpool_. And Deadpool narrates the trailer.  
    *    Confirmed. Ryan Reynolds even pitches in for the trailer.

*   _Mighty Morphin' Power Rangers: The Movie_ for the release of _Power Rangers (2017)_:  
    *    From the franchise created by Haim Saban that was based on a Japanese TV show, that was passed down to Disney, to Nick, which didn't get better until Dino Charge, that would eventually be handed over to Lionsgate, comes the very first _Power Rangers_ Movie with the one memeno one could be allowed to forget unless is sounds completely badass. "Mighty Morphin' Power Rangers: The Movie".  
    *    Starring: The Multicolored Ranger (Tommy), Before he was Rambo (Rocky), Once a Ranger, Always a Ranger (Adam), Bill-I, the Science Guy (Billy), Sometimes Layla (Aisha), Kim Possible (Kimberly), The Secret of the Ooze (Ivan Ooze), Jack Skullington, (Skull), Bulkhead (Bulk), Number III (Alpha), Put the "On" in "Zordon" (Zordon), and Ursula (Rita Repulsa).  
        *    Or they could do the entire Power Rangers Series, possibly with a trailer for the Roast of the Power Rangers.  
        *    Confirmed.

    *    Starring: Lick-Lick-Lick My Balls! (Lickety Split), Barney (Spike), The Wind Rises (Wind Whistler), Little Orphan Annie (Morning Glory), Sundance Film Festival (Sundance), Bart Simpson (Gusty), Button Mash (Buttons), Bryant Grundle (Grundle King), Bulk and Skull (Reeka and Draggle), The Lost Sanderson Sister (Hydia), Jack Chick (Moochick), Gak (Smooze), Insert Spider-Man Joke Here (Ahgg), Disney Creatures of the Farce (woodland animals), and Megan Fox (Megan).

        *    Starring: Separatist Terminator (Durge), The White Witch (Asajj Ventress), The only way Sam Jackson looks cool (Mace Windu fighting Droids single-handedly), Wheezer Ver. 1 (General Grievous), Green-Skinned Percy Jackson (Kit Fisto), Wolf Man? (Voolvif Monn), Biker Guys in a joust (The jousting battle), the most hated Padawan in history (Barriss Offee), Hay-Didn't act again for this one (Anakin), Ewan 2D animation, The disposable duo (Roron Corobb and Foul Moudama), and Damage Control (Heavily-armed Clone Troopers).  
        *    Confirmed.

*    One of the 1990s _Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles_ movies or the _TMNT_ CGI movie to coincide with the upcoming Ninja Turtles movie.  
    *    Jossed. They did the _Coming Out of Our Shells_ Tour instead.

*    A _Disney Channel Original Movie_ for _Adventures in Babysitting (2016)_.  
    *    Jossed, though it doesn't hurt for them to do the original _Adventures in Babysitting_ sometime.

*   _Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice_  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _The Bourne Series_: For the release of _Jason Bourne_. And the Honest Trailer will make a jab at _The Bourne Legacy_.  
    *    Confirmed for the first three movies; jab at _The Bourne Legacy_ and all.

*   _Watchmen (2009)_  
    *    Confirmed.

*    The Emmy Awards: If so, then it would be the first TV award to get an Honest Trailer.  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _Alvin and the Chipmunks (Film Series)_: Epic Voice Guy's voice gets chipmunked.  
    *    Starring: Dramatic Chipmunk (Alvin, Simon, and Theodore), A _My Name Is Earl_ Actor (Dave Seville), DavidNot Bowie (Ian Hawke), Your _Glee_ Actor (Gail), Britney Spears (Claire Wilson), and Shopper's Girl (Mother in Store)

*   _Captain America: Civil War_  
    *    Starring: Barnes & Noble (Bucky and Captain America), Holla! (Black Panther), The AmazingSony-Man (Spider-Man), Sherlock Holmes (Iron Man), Melisandre (Wanda), Put a Bird on It (The Falcon), Generic Marvel Villain (Zemo) and Brian Fantanta (Ant-Man)  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _The Divergent Series: Allegiant_ (aka _Detergent's Stupid Crappyness: Bore & Order_ *CHUNG-CHUNG*)  
    *    Jon Bailey interrupts his reading finding this movie is identical to _Maze Runner: The Scorch Trials_.  
    *    Starring: Cyber Internet Cosplay (Beatrice Prior), Mr. Fantastic (Peter), I Give Up (Tori), Toast (Christina), How S**t That Was (Tobias), Princess Diana (Evelyn), A Wasted _The Martian_ Actor (David) and Teenage Mutant Augusts Turtle (Caleb)
Advertisement:
*    Something from Blue Sky Studios. Most likely one of the _Ice Age_ or the _Rio_ movies.  
*    A Netflix original series, preferable _House of Cards_ or _Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt_.  
    *    Confirmed for both _House of Cards_ and _Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt_, as part of the Honest Trailer for the Emmys.

*   _Independence Day: Resurgence_: The trailer will be packed of jokes about the film not holding up to _Independence Day_.  
    *    Starring: Yakko Warner (David Levinson), Vivica is Still Not Actually a Fox (Jasmine Dubrow), Jabberjaw (Dr. Brackish Okun), Buzz Lightyear Plus (the two astronauts in the movie), Marilyn Monroe's Sister (Patricia Whitmore), Cher (Rain), Chris Hemsworth's Son (Jake Morrison), Ralph Fiennes (General Adams), Bobby's World (Bobby) and How Do You Know That the F#$@k Is That (Dr. Catherine Marceaux)  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _Pitch Perfect 2_  
*   _Spider-Man: The Animated Series_: For the release of _Spider-Man: Homecoming_.  
*   _The Powerpuff Girls Movie_  
*    All the _Ben 10_ installments  
*   _Fatal Attraction_: For the release of _Fifty Shades Darker_  
*   _Basic Instinct_  
*   _Finding Dory_  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _The Legend of Tarzan_  
*   _The BFG_  
*   _Pete's Dragon (1977)_: For the 2016 remake.  
*   _Ghostbusters (2016)_: Epic Voice Guy might call out on both sides of the Unpleasable Fanbase of the movie for their bias and accusations on each other over why they love or hate the movie only to go Oh, Crap! when both sides go after him because he thought the movie was neither great or bad but So Okay, It's Average.  
    *    Confirmed. It even did consider it So Okay, It's Average ("fine, but forgettable"), but overall it took the side of saying it was a bad movie ("It's not as bad as they said that it was gonna be, but still, it... it's still pretty bad"), and went "Oh Crap!" too ("I'm _so_ getting doxxed!"). They even disabled comments.

*    Either _Stranger Things_ or _Gravity Falls_ when _Stranger Things_ Season 2 premieres.  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _The Wolverine_ when _Logan_ comes out.  
    *    Jossed. It came out ahead of _Deadpool & Wolverine_ instead.

*   _The Room (2003)_ when _The Disaster Artist_ comes out.  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _Get Out (2017)_  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _The Book of Life_ for when _Coco_ comes out.  
    *    Jossed.

*   _Thor: Ragnarok_. Expect the following:  
    *    The Narrator struggles to pronounce Taika Waititi's name before settling on "KiwiJamesGunn" or "New Zealand's second most famous director.  
    *    The Narrator going over the similarities and differences between _Ragnarok_, _Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2_, and _Captain America: Civil War_ (inclusion of other heroes, dysfunctional team dynamics, etc.). Bonus points if they conclude with a Call-Back to their video for _Guardians of the Galaxy (2014)_ by saying something like "I guess it's not stealing if they are doing it to themselves."  
    *    The Narrator gushing over the Kirbyesqueaesthetic.  
    *    Confirmed for the Honest Trailer, and regarding the expectations: Jossed, sort of (they point jumping off one vehicle to hit another vehicle that's behind is in all those movies, but that's it), and confirmed.

    *    Starring: Jason Stake-'Em (Billy Butcher), Hugh Dorkman (Hughie), Justice League Barbie (Starlight), Captain MAGA (Homelander), XenaOnatopp (Queen Maeve), I Snark In Your General Direction (Frenchie), Milk Fury (Mother's Milk), Laura Kill-ey (the Female), Anthony Quickie (A-Train), Prawn Jeremy (the Deep), A Frank Miller Type (Black Noir), Thanos (Translucent's death scene), and Lactation Luthor (Stilwell).  
    *    Confirmed under the Honest Title of _All Super-Cops are Bastards_.

*   _Frozen II_ (aka _The Last Icebender_)  
    *    Starring: Avatar Elsa (Elsa), Anna of Rohirrim (Anna), REO Speedsled (Kristoff during "Lost in the Woods"), Ice-istential Crisis (Olaf), Nick Fury (General Mattias), The Colors of the Wind (Gale the wind spirit), Pas-Calcifer (Bruni the salamander), War-ter Horse (the Nokk), Rockbiter (the Rock Giants), and An Ass-Load of Callbacks (Elsa's memories in Ahtohallan)  
    *    Confirmed under the Honest Title of _Rise of Icewalker_.

    *    Confirmed, with Season 1 under the Honest Title of _The Outer Rim Job_ and Season 2 under the Honest Title of _The Masked Slinger_.

*   _Interspecies Reviewers_ (aka _The Bitcher_)

    *    Jossed.

*   _The Real Snyder Cut_  
    *    Confirmed.

*   _The World's End_ (aka _The Fault in Our Bars_)

    *    Confirmed under the Honest Title _Teenage Mutants Facing Hurdles_.

*   _KonoSuba_ (aka _Ah! My Goddess Sucks_)  
*   _Re:Zero_ (aka _Happy Desu Day_)  
*   _Overlord (2012)_ (aka _Things Mr Suzuki Is Not Allowed To Do In A MMORPG_)  
*   _The Saga of Tanya the Evil_ (aka _Goebbels Girl_)  
*   _Isekai Quartet_ (aka _School Days_)  
*   _Zombie Land Saga_ (aka _Night of theLove Live-ing Dead_)  
*   _Hamilton_ on Disney+ (aka _This is America_)  
*    The _Monty Python_ films (aka _Tales of the Unexpected_)  
    *    They'll most likely cover, _Monty Python and the Holy Grail_, _Monty Python's Life of Brian_ and _Monty Python's the Meaning of Life_, with brief mentions of _And Now For Something Completely Different_, _Monty Python Live at the Hollywood Bowl_ and _Monty Python Live (Mostly): One Down, Five to Go_.  
    *    "From a comedy trope of five, well-educatedBritishcomedians. And one American".  
    *    For _The Holy Grail_, mentions will go out on how low budget the film was, to such an extent that "horses were just knights pretending to ride, while a guy behind knocks two halves of a coconut together", the same castle was used from different angles and that the film's "big battle ending instead is instead replaced, with King Arthur and his loyal knights getting arrested for taking LARP too far".  
    *    For _Life of Brian_, it'll be introduced as "a film so controversial, it got banned in Norway!", and maybe the narrator will mistakenly call it "Life of Brain", before being corrected (cut away to someone shouting "Brian! Brian! Brian!", and the narrator replying, "oh, sorry"). Then, it'll be mentioned that George Harrison funded the film and the song "Always Look on the Bright Side of Life" is "the song every Brit will want sung at their funeral".  
    *    For _The Meaning of Life_, they'll state Mr. Creosote as being "so gruesome, it grossed out Quentin Tarantino!"  
    *    They'll even use the phrase, "And now for something completely different".  

        *    Confirmed for _Monty Python and the Holy Grail_ as _The Whitest Brits U Know_.

_**The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie**_ is a 2004 American animated adventure comedy film co-written and directed by Stephen Hillenburg. Based on the television series _SpongeBob SquarePants_ created by Hillenburg, the film features the series' regular voice cast, including Tom Kenny, Bill Fagerbakke, Clancy Brown, Rodger Bumpass and Mr. Lawrence, who are joined by Alec Baldwin, Scarlett Johansson and Jeffrey Tambor, with David Hasselhoff appearing in live action as himself. In the film, SpongeBob with Patrick sets out on a quest to Shell City to retrieve King Neptune's stolen crown, exonerate his boss Mr. Krabs, stop Plankton, and prove his manhood.
Hillenburg accepted an offer for a film adaptation of _SpongeBob SquarePants_ from Paramount Pictures in 2002, after turning it down multiple times the previous year. He assembled a team from the show's writing staff, including himself, Derek Drymon, Tim Hill, Kent Osborne, Aaron Springer and Paul Tibbitt, and structured the film as a mythical [hero's journey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hero's_journey "Hero's journey") that would bring SpongeBob and Patrick to the surface. The film was originally intended to serve as the series finale, but due to its financial success, the show continued. Tibbitt took Hillenburg's place as showrunner afterwards.
_The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_ premiered at the [Grauman's Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman's_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre") on November 14, 2004, and was released in the United States on November 19 by Paramount. It received generally positive reviews and grossed $141 million on a $30 million budget. It is the first in a series of _SpongeBob_ films.

Mr. Krabs opens a second location of the Krusty Krab, right next to the original. His fry cook, SpongeBob SquarePants, hopes to be promoted to manager of the new restaurant, but Krabs instead selects his co-worker, Squidward Tentacles, explaining to SpongeBob that he is a "kid" who is too young and immature to handle the position. Depressed, SpongeBob goes to the Goofy Goober ice cream parlor, where he indulges himself with ice cream with his best friend Patrick Star and wakes up the following morning with a hangover.
Krabs' rival Plankton, owner of the Chum Bucket restaurant, initiates "Plan Z" in an attempt to obtain the Krabby Patty secret formula and take over the world. He steals King Neptune's crown, sends it to a place called Shell City, and frames Krabs for the theft. Neptune confronts Krabs about his stolen crown and is convinced of Krabs' guilt when a hungover SpongeBob smears him. Recovering from his hangover, SpongeBob promises Neptune that he will retrieve the crown from Shell City. Neptune freezes Krabs until further notice, telling SpongeBob to return in ten days (until Patrick argues it down to six) or Krabs will be executed. Neptune's daughter, Mindy, encourages SpongeBob and Patrick but warns them of dangers surrounding Shell City, including "the Cyclops", a monster who kidnaps sea creatures.
SpongeBob and Patrick head for Shell City in the Patty Wagon, a Krabby Patty-shaped car stored underneath the restaurant. After the duo leave Bikini Bottom, Plankton steals the formula from the frozen Krabs and uses it to sell Krabby Patties. He distributes free helmets with the Krabby Patties that brainwash customers into doing Plankton's bidding, subsequently taking over Bikini Bottom and hiring a hitman named Dennis to prevent SpongeBob and Patrick from returning with the crown.

SpongeBob and Patrick encounter a hazardous trench, lose the Patty Wagon, and contemplate giving up. Mindy, whom Patrick has a crush on, appears and encourages them by applying fake mustaches made of seaweed, convincing them that she magically turned them from kids into men. Armed with newfound confidence, the two successfully traverse the trench and encounter Dennis on the other side. He demonstrates that the mustaches are fake, and prepares to squash the duo with his boot but is suddenly stepped on by a much larger boot belonging to the "Cyclops", a human diver, who abducts SpongeBob and Patrick.
The duo are placed under a heat lamp by the Cyclops, learning that they have arrived in "Shell City", a gift shop selling dried sea creatures. Proud that they reached their destination, they shed tears just before getting dried up, which short-circuit the lamp and activate the emergency sprinklers, reviving the two alongside the other dried sea creatures. While the sea creatures attack the Cyclops, SpongeBob and Patrick take the crown to the beach, where David Hasselhoff offers them a ride home. Dennis catches up and fights them on Hasselhoff's back, ultimately falling into the sea as Hasselhoff passes under a catamaran.
Neptune arrives to execute Krabs, but SpongeBob and Patrick return with the crown just in time. Plankton drops a mind-control helmet on Neptune and surrounds SpongeBob, Patrick and Mindy with his army of slaves. SpongeBob, embracing the fact that he's accomplished so much despite being a kid, uses the power of rock and roll to play "Goofy Goober Rock", freeing Neptune and the citizens of Bikini Bottom from Plankton's control.
As Plankton is arrested by the police, Neptune unfreezes Krabs and the two make amends. Krabs then appoints SpongeBob as the manager of the Krusty Krab 2.

_The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_ was long-planned,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-RDS-8) as Nickelodeon and Paramount Pictures had approached to series creator Stephen Hillenburg for a film based on _SpongeBob SquarePants_, but he refused for more than a year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel1-9) Hillenburg was concerned, after watching _The Iron Giant_ and _Toy Story_ with his son, about the challenge of SpongeBob and Patrick doing something more cinematically consequential and inspiring without losing what he called the SpongeBob "cadence".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel1-9) Hillenburg believed that the film's story "had to be SpongeBob in a great adventure. That's where the comedy's coming from, having these two naïve characters, SpongeBob and Patrick, a doofus and an idiot, on this incredibly dangerous heroic odyssey with all the odds against them."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel1-9)
> I never wanted to do a movie because I didn't think that what we wanted to say needed to be in a movie. I like the short form for animation. Then this story idea came up that lent itself to a longer format. You can't do a road trip adventure in a short form.

In 2002, Hillenburg and the show's staff stopped making episodes to work on the film after the show's third season was completed.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-EVT-10) When news of production on the film was announced, the show's staff made a joke plot for the film which had SpongeBob rescue Patrick from a fisherman in Florida;[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-EVT-10) a reference to the plot of _Finding Nemo_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-EVT-10) Hillenburg directed and produced the film, and also co-wrote the screenplay with five other writer-animators from the show (Paul Tibbitt, Derek Drymon, Aaron Springer, Kent Osborne and Tim Hill) over a three-month period in a room of a former Glendale, California bank.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel1-9) At the beginning of the series, Hillenburg screened a number of silent shorts (from Laurel and Hardy, Charlie Chaplin and Buster Keaton) and work by two modern comic actors: Jerry Lewis and Pee-wee Herman, both obvious inspirations for SpongeBob.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel2-11) For the film, the writers created a mythical hero's quest: the search for a stolen crown, which brings SpongeBob and Patrick to the surface.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel2-11)Bill Fagerbakke (the voice of Patrick) said about the plot, "It's just nuts. I'm continually dazzled and delighted with what these guys came up with."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-AbsorbingTales-12)

The film features live-action scenes directed by Mark Osborne in Santa Monica, California.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-AbsorbingTales-12)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Replica1-34) The ship used during the 30-second opening featuring the pirates singing the theme song was the _Bounty_,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Bounty1-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-36) a 180-foot-long (55 m), enlarged reconstruction of the 1787 Royal Navy sailing ship HMS _Bounty_ built for _Mutiny on the Bounty_ (1962). The ship appeared in a number of other films, including _Treasure Island_ (1999), _[Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pirates\_of\_the\_Caribbean:\_Dead\_Man's\_Chest "Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest")_ (2006) and _[Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pirates\_of\_the\_Caribbean:\_At\_World's\_End "Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End")_ (2007).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-38) In film trailers, live-action scenes were taken from _Das Boot_ (1981), _The Hunt for Red October_ (1990) and _U-571_ (2000).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-EVT-10)
The crew built a larger-than-life replica of David Hasselhoff as his double in filming the fight scene with Dennis.

David Hasselhoff made a cameo appearance in the live-action scenes, offering SpongeBob and Patrick a ride to Bikini Bottom.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-LAS1-39) The scene was originally written before consulting Hasselhoff.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets1-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets2-41) Hillenburg was pleased with the storyboards;[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-OralHistory-13) Lead storyboard artist Sherm Cohen noted the positive reaction among the film's storyboard artists after Hillenburg brought up the animatic of the scene.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-OralHistory-13) Hillenburg and the staff were counting on casting Hasselhoff, who eventually agreed before seeing the script.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets1-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets2-41) Hillenburg said about the actor, "He's a great guy. ...He was great at making fun of himself."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets1-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets2-41)

The crew built a 750-pound (340 kg), 12-foot (3.7 m) replica of Hasselhoff.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Replica1-34)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-LAS1-39)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-42) The $100,000 replica was kept at Hasselhoff's home after completion of filming;[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-LAS2-43) he has said, "It freaked me out because it was so lifelike, with teeth, when you touch it it feels like real skin."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-LAS2-43) Hasselhoff filmed in cold water, where he was pulled by a sled nine yards across the sea.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-AbsorbingTales-12)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-LAS1-39)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-InsidePineapple-31)

In late March 2014, Hasselhoff offered the replica up for auction with other memorabilia collected during his career. [Julien's Auctions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien's_Auctions "Julien's Auctions") handled the item's sale, which was expected to bring in between $20,000 and $30,000. Ultimately, Hasselhoff pulled the item, just a few days before the auction.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-44)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-45)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-46)
Animatic of deleted scene, with SpongeBob and Patrick (right) encountering Sandy Cheeks (left) on the surface
The DVD and Blu-ray releases include animatics of deleted scenes from the film, including SpongeBob and Patrick's meeting with Sandy Cheeks (a squirrel) on the surface after they escape from Shell City.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-DeletedScenes-47) Patrick repeatedly vomits, upset by Sandy's unusual appearance.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-DeletedScenes-47) Sandy is pursued by black-suited exterminators,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-DeletedScenes-47) and defends herself with acorns.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-DeletedScenes-47) She informs SpongeBob and Patrick that they can return to Bikini Bottom by taking a bus at the beach.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-DeletedScenes-47) This idea was later used for the second film _The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water_ (2015), where Sandy became a giant realistic squirrel.

Title: The 6 Most Unexpected Celebrities Who Showed Up In 'SpongeBob' Movies
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6
In the wide world of American cartoons, there’s no larger name than _SpongeBob SquarePants_(1999-Present). For over a quarter of a century, SpongeBob has delighted kids and adults, whether it be through silly jokes, gross-out humor, or clever adult jokes. Most kids can easily identify the voices of Tom Kenny, Bill Fagerbakke, and Clancy Browne as SpongeBob, Patrick, and Mr. Krabs, respectively. Still, in several _SpongeBob SquarePants_ movies, you may hear or see celebrities that you probably weren’t expecting.
Some celebrities decide to appear in _SpongeBob SquarePants_ to delight their kids. Some do it for a paycheck. Regardless of the reasons why, nobody was really expecting these six celebrities to appear in a _SpongeBob SquarePants_ movie. The upcoming _The SpongBob SquarePants Movie: The Search For SquarePants_(2025) will most likely contain a treasure trove of weird and delightful celebrity cameos, so let’s take a look at some of the most unexpected celebrities to appear in a _SpongeBob_ movie. All of these films can either be found on Paramount+ or Netflix, so head over there if you want to see some bizarrely iconic cameos.

## David Hasselhoff - The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie (2004)
Arguably, the most iconic cameo in all of the franchise would be the moment when the legendary David Hasselhoff, star of _Knight Rider_(1982-1986) and _Baywatch_(1989-2001), came running across the screen to save SpongeBob and Patrick from dehydration.
Hasselhoff’s kids loved the series, so when he was offered the opportunity to play a more exaggerated version of his character from _Baywatch,_ he jumped at the opportunity. His appearance was an instant hit with adults and kids alike. Kids loved watching this ridiculous man swim like a speedboat across the water, while adults got a kick out of seeing the most-watched man on TV act as a cartoony caricature of himself. To this day, Hasselhoff’s appearance in _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_has made him a memorable part of the franchise, to the point where he has cameoed in later _SpongeBob_ projects, including the recent video game _SpongeBob SquarePants: Titans of the Tide._

## Scarlett Johansson - The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie (2004)
Nowadays, most people know who Scarlett Johansson is. Between her tenure in the MCU as Black Widow, her award-winning performances in _Marriage Story_(2019), and her recent box office behemoth _Jurassic World Rebirth_(2025)_,_ she needs no introduction.
Back in 2004, that was hardly the case. While she gained prominence the year before thanks to _Lost In Translation_(2003)_,_ Scarlett Johansson was relatively unknown, especially in the realm of voice acting. Nevertheless, she voiced King Neptune’s daughter, Princess Mindy, in _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie,_ who helped SpongeBob and Patrick on their quest to retrieve her father’s crown. Her cameo is still a surprising reveal to longtime fans, since she was rarely featured in the marketing in the lead-up to the film’s release, and in part because of how she quickly catapulted into the realm of Hollywood A-Lister in the decades that followed. But looking back, this helped introduce her to a mainstream audience and would only be another step in her meteoric rise to stardom.

## Alec Baldwin - The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie (2004)
Rounding out our trio of notable celebrity cameos in _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_ would be the man who played Dennis, the imposing and dangerous bounty hunter sent to hunt down SpongeBob and Patrick, portrayed by Alec Baldwin.
While Baldwin’s star has dimmed significantly since the release of the film, and mostly in part due to the controversy surrounding the filming of _Rust_(2024), he’s nevertheless a well-known name within the world of cinema. While he’s mostly known for his sardonic wit, seeing him play an intimidating bounty hunter actually manages to work pretty well, channeling a performance that takes some cues from Slade from _Teen Titans_(2003-2007). It’s unexpected to see such an A-list actor play this relatively silent menace, but leave it to Alec Baldwin to get the most out of what should be a simple villain.

## Keanu Reeves - The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run (2020)
For most of the 2010s, Keanu Reeves was seen as the perennial Hollywood badass. Thanks to the popularity of _John Wick_(2014), as well as a breathtaking performance in the video game _Cyberpunk 2077,_ Keanu Reeves was all the rage. So much so that his cameo in _The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run_seemed inevitable.
In it, Keanu Reeves plays a spirit inhabiting a tumbleweed who was meant to guide SpongeBob and Patrick on their journey to rescue Gary. He pops up intermittently to offer courage, positive reinforcement, and the kind of platitudes that you would expect from mentors like Splinter in _Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles_(1987-1996). However, there’s no getting around the fact that just seeing Keanu Reeves’ face inside a tumbleweed is bizarre. Apparently, the role was conceived solely for Reeves, so the uncanny appearance is intentional and part of the joke. It certainly does leave an impact and is probably the most memorable thing about the film, making it just as surprising as Hasselhoff’s role in _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie._

## Johnny Knoxville - Saving Bikini Bottom: The Sandy Cheeks Movie (2024)
While there have only been four theatrically released _SpongeBob SquarePants_ movies, there have been a few direct-to-streaming feature films that have their own odd and unexpected celebrity cameos. Probably the most unexpected one would have to be Johnny Knoxville appearing as Sandy’s brother Randy in _Saving Bikini Bottom: The Sandy Cheeks Movie_.
While this isn’t Knoxville’s first appearance in the franchise, his role as Randy will definitely be nostalgic to those who remember watching Knoxville on _Jackass_(2000-2001). Randy works at a rodeo and dresses like an Evel Knievel knock-off, and he, alongside the rest of Sandy’s family, helps Sandy and SpongeBob save Bikini Bottom. Even for the little time he’s present in this 82-minute movie, Knoxville shows that he’s grown and matured since his younger days. He’s less obnoxious, and seeing his character lean into what made Knoxville such a fun presence in his early years lets you appreciate Knoxville’s appearance all the more.

## Ice Spice - The SpongeBob Movie: The Search For SquarePants (2025)
It’s not uncommon for animated movies to get a tie-in pop song from a popular artist. Plenty of films have done it, yet seeing Ice Spice not only produce the lead single for _The SpongeBob Movie: The Search For SquarePants_, the infectiously catchy “Big Guy,” and appear as a character is pretty unexpected.
If you’re a fan of her music, though, that shouldn’t be too big of a shock. After all, one of her first singles was titled “Bikini Bottom,” and she talks about how she grew up watching the series. Say what you will about her talent as an artist, but seeing a younger celebrity cameo in a franchise like _SpongeBob SquarePants_ makes perfect sense. Ice Spice herself has also been dipping her toes into acting this year as well, with her recently cameoing in Spike Lee’s _Highest 2 Lowest_ (2025).
Thanks to Nickelodeon’s marketing machine, it’s impossible to separate Ice Spice from _The Search For SquarePants_, and even if she’s only in the movie as much as Johnny Knoxville was in _Saving Bikini Bottom: The Sandy Cheeks Movie,_ that’ll probably be the case for years to come.

texts.2:
_**The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie**_ is a 2004 American animated adventure comedy film co-written and directed by Stephen Hillenburg. Based on the television series _SpongeBob SquarePants_ created by Hillenburg, the film features the series' regular voice cast, including Tom Kenny, Bill Fagerbakke, Clancy Brown, Rodger Bumpass and Mr. Lawrence, who are joined by Alec Baldwin, Scarlett Johansson and Jeffrey Tambor, with David Hasselhoff appearing in live action as himself. In the film, SpongeBob with Patrick sets out on a quest to Shell City to retrieve King Neptune's stolen crown, exonerate his boss Mr. Krabs, stop Plankton, and prove his manhood.
Hillenburg accepted an offer for a film adaptation of _SpongeBob SquarePants_ from Paramount Pictures in 2002, after turning it down multiple times the previous year. He assembled a team from the show's writing staff, including himself, Derek Drymon, Tim Hill, Kent Osborne, Aaron Springer and Paul Tibbitt, and structured the film as a mythical [hero's journey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hero's_journey "Hero's journey") that would bring SpongeBob and Patrick to the surface. The film was originally intended to serve as the series finale, but due to its financial success, the show continued. Tibbitt took Hillenburg's place as showrunner afterwards.
_The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_ premiered at the [Grauman's Chinese Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grauman's_Chinese_Theatre "Grauman's Chinese Theatre") on November 14, 2004, and was released in the United States on November 19 by Paramount. It received generally positive reviews and grossed $141 million on a $30 million budget. It is the first in a series of _SpongeBob_ films.
texts.3:
Mr. Krabs opens a second location of the Krusty Krab, right next to the original. His fry cook, SpongeBob SquarePants, hopes to be promoted to manager of the new restaurant, but Krabs instead selects his co-worker, Squidward Tentacles, explaining to SpongeBob that he is a "kid" who is too young and immature to handle the position. Depressed, SpongeBob goes to the Goofy Goober ice cream parlor, where he indulges himself with ice cream with his best friend Patrick Star and wakes up the following morning with a hangover.
Krabs' rival Plankton, owner of the Chum Bucket restaurant, initiates "Plan Z" in an attempt to obtain the Krabby Patty secret formula and take over the world. He steals King Neptune's crown, sends it to a place called Shell City, and frames Krabs for the theft. Neptune confronts Krabs about his stolen crown and is convinced of Krabs' guilt when a hungover SpongeBob smears him. Recovering from his hangover, SpongeBob promises Neptune that he will retrieve the crown from Shell City. Neptune freezes Krabs until further notice, telling SpongeBob to return in ten days (until Patrick argues it down to six) or Krabs will be executed. Neptune's daughter, Mindy, encourages SpongeBob and Patrick but warns them of dangers surrounding Shell City, including "the Cyclops", a monster who kidnaps sea creatures.
SpongeBob and Patrick head for Shell City in the Patty Wagon, a Krabby Patty-shaped car stored underneath the restaurant. After the duo leave Bikini Bottom, Plankton steals the formula from the frozen Krabs and uses it to sell Krabby Patties. He distributes free helmets with the Krabby Patties that brainwash customers into doing Plankton's bidding, subsequently taking over Bikini Bottom and hiring a hitman named Dennis to prevent SpongeBob and Patrick from returning with the crown.
texts.4:
SpongeBob and Patrick encounter a hazardous trench, lose the Patty Wagon, and contemplate giving up. Mindy, whom Patrick has a crush on, appears and encourages them by applying fake mustaches made of seaweed, convincing them that she magically turned them from kids into men. Armed with newfound confidence, the two successfully traverse the trench and encounter Dennis on the other side. He demonstrates that the mustaches are fake, and prepares to squash the duo with his boot but is suddenly stepped on by a much larger boot belonging to the "Cyclops", a human diver, who abducts SpongeBob and Patrick.
The duo are placed under a heat lamp by the Cyclops, learning that they have arrived in "Shell City", a gift shop selling dried sea creatures. Proud that they reached their destination, they shed tears just before getting dried up, which short-circuit the lamp and activate the emergency sprinklers, reviving the two alongside the other dried sea creatures. While the sea creatures attack the Cyclops, SpongeBob and Patrick take the crown to the beach, where David Hasselhoff offers them a ride home. Dennis catches up and fights them on Hasselhoff's back, ultimately falling into the sea as Hasselhoff passes under a catamaran.
Neptune arrives to execute Krabs, but SpongeBob and Patrick return with the crown just in time. Plankton drops a mind-control helmet on Neptune and surrounds SpongeBob, Patrick and Mindy with his army of slaves. SpongeBob, embracing the fact that he's accomplished so much despite being a kid, uses the power of rock and roll to play "Goofy Goober Rock", freeing Neptune and the citizens of Bikini Bottom from Plankton's control.
As Plankton is arrested by the police, Neptune unfreezes Krabs and the two make amends. Krabs then appoints SpongeBob as the manager of the Krusty Krab 2.

*   Aaron Hendry as the Cyclops (in-suit performer)
In a mid-credits scene, Mageina Tovah portrays a theater usher.
texts.6:
_The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_ was long-planned,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-RDS-8) as Nickelodeon and Paramount Pictures had approached to series creator Stephen Hillenburg for a film based on _SpongeBob SquarePants_, but he refused for more than a year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel1-9) Hillenburg was concerned, after watching _The Iron Giant_ and _Toy Story_ with his son, about the challenge of SpongeBob and Patrick doing something more cinematically consequential and inspiring without losing what he called the SpongeBob "cadence".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel1-9) Hillenburg believed that the film's story "had to be SpongeBob in a great adventure. That's where the comedy's coming from, having these two naïve characters, SpongeBob and Patrick, a doofus and an idiot, on this incredibly dangerous heroic odyssey with all the odds against them."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel1-9)
> I never wanted to do a movie because I didn't think that what we wanted to say needed to be in a movie. I like the short form for animation. Then this story idea came up that lent itself to a longer format. You can't do a road trip adventure in a short form.
texts.7: In 2002, Hillenburg and the show's staff stopped making episodes to work on the film after the show's third season was completed.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-EVT-10) When news of production on the film was announced, the show's staff made a joke plot for the film which had SpongeBob rescue Patrick from a fisherman in Florida;[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-EVT-10) a reference to the plot of _Finding Nemo_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-EVT-10) Hillenburg directed and produced the film, and also co-wrote the screenplay with five other writer-animators from the show (Paul Tibbitt, Derek Drymon, Aaron Springer, Kent Osborne and Tim Hill) over a three-month period in a room of a former Glendale, California bank.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel1-9) At the beginning of the series, Hillenburg screened a number of silent shorts (from Laurel and Hardy, Charlie Chaplin and Buster Keaton) and work by two modern comic actors: Jerry Lewis and Pee-wee Herman, both obvious inspirations for SpongeBob.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel2-11) For the film, the writers created a mythical hero's quest: the search for a stolen crown, which brings SpongeBob and Patrick to the surface.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Edel2-11)Bill Fagerbakke (the voice of Patrick) said about the plot, "It's just nuts. I'm continually dazzled and delighted with what these guys came up with."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-AbsorbingTales-12)
texts.13:
The film features live-action scenes directed by Mark Osborne in Santa Monica, California.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-AbsorbingTales-12)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Replica1-34) The ship used during the 30-second opening featuring the pirates singing the theme song was the _Bounty_,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Bounty1-35)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-36) a 180-foot-long (55 m), enlarged reconstruction of the 1787 Royal Navy sailing ship HMS _Bounty_ built for _Mutiny on the Bounty_ (1962). The ship appeared in a number of other films, including _Treasure Island_ (1999), _[Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pirates\_of\_the\_Caribbean:\_Dead\_Man's\_Chest "Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest")_ (2006) and _[Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pirates\_of\_the\_Caribbean:\_At\_World's\_End "Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End")_ (2007).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-38) In film trailers, live-action scenes were taken from _Das Boot_ (1981), _The Hunt for Red October_ (1990) and _U-571_ (2000).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-EVT-10)
The crew built a larger-than-life replica of David Hasselhoff as his double in filming the fight scene with Dennis.
texts.14: David Hasselhoff made a cameo appearance in the live-action scenes, offering SpongeBob and Patrick a ride to Bikini Bottom.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-LAS1-39) The scene was originally written before consulting Hasselhoff.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets1-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets2-41) Hillenburg was pleased with the storyboards;[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-OralHistory-13) Lead storyboard artist Sherm Cohen noted the positive reaction among the film's storyboard artists after Hillenburg brought up the animatic of the scene.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-OralHistory-13) Hillenburg and the staff were counting on casting Hasselhoff, who eventually agreed before seeing the script.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets1-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets2-41) Hillenburg said about the actor, "He's a great guy. ...He was great at making fun of himself."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets1-40)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-10Secrets2-41)
texts.15: The crew built a 750-pound (340 kg), 12-foot (3.7 m) replica of Hasselhoff.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-Replica1-34)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-LAS1-39)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-42) The $100,000 replica was kept at Hasselhoff's home after completion of filming;[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-LAS2-43) he has said, "It freaked me out because it was so lifelike, with teeth, when you touch it it feels like real skin."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-LAS2-43) Hasselhoff filmed in cold water, where he was pulled by a sled nine yards across the sea.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-AbsorbingTales-12)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-LAS1-39)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-InsidePineapple-31)
texts.16:
In late March 2014, Hasselhoff offered the replica up for auction with other memorabilia collected during his career. [Julien's Auctions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien's_Auctions "Julien's Auctions") handled the item's sale, which was expected to bring in between $20,000 and $30,000. Ultimately, Hasselhoff pulled the item, just a few days before the auction.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-44)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-45)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-46)
Animatic of deleted scene, with SpongeBob and Patrick (right) encountering Sandy Cheeks (left) on the surface
The DVD and Blu-ray releases include animatics of deleted scenes from the film, including SpongeBob and Patrick's meeting with Sandy Cheeks (a squirrel) on the surface after they escape from Shell City.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-DeletedScenes-47) Patrick repeatedly vomits, upset by Sandy's unusual appearance.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-DeletedScenes-47) Sandy is pursued by black-suited exterminators,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-DeletedScenes-47) and defends herself with acorns.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-DeletedScenes-47) She informs SpongeBob and Patrick that they can return to Bikini Bottom by taking a bus at the beach.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_SpongeBob_SquarePants_Movie#cite_note-DeletedScenes-47) This idea was later used for the second film _The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water_ (2015), where Sandy became a giant realistic squirrel.

texts.0:
In the wide world of American cartoons, there’s no larger name than _SpongeBob SquarePants_(1999-Present). For over a quarter of a century, SpongeBob has delighted kids and adults, whether it be through silly jokes, gross-out humor, or clever adult jokes. Most kids can easily identify the voices of Tom Kenny, Bill Fagerbakke, and Clancy Browne as SpongeBob, Patrick, and Mr. Krabs, respectively. Still, in several _SpongeBob SquarePants_ movies, you may hear or see celebrities that you probably weren’t expecting.
Some celebrities decide to appear in _SpongeBob SquarePants_ to delight their kids. Some do it for a paycheck. Regardless of the reasons why, nobody was really expecting these six celebrities to appear in a _SpongeBob SquarePants_ movie. The upcoming _The SpongBob SquarePants Movie: The Search For SquarePants_(2025) will most likely contain a treasure trove of weird and delightful celebrity cameos, so let’s take a look at some of the most unexpected celebrities to appear in a _SpongeBob_ movie. All of these films can either be found on Paramount+ or Netflix, so head over there if you want to see some bizarrely iconic cameos.
texts.1:
## David Hasselhoff - The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie (2004)
Arguably, the most iconic cameo in all of the franchise would be the moment when the legendary David Hasselhoff, star of _Knight Rider_(1982-1986) and _Baywatch_(1989-2001), came running across the screen to save SpongeBob and Patrick from dehydration.
Hasselhoff’s kids loved the series, so when he was offered the opportunity to play a more exaggerated version of his character from _Baywatch,_ he jumped at the opportunity. His appearance was an instant hit with adults and kids alike. Kids loved watching this ridiculous man swim like a speedboat across the water, while adults got a kick out of seeing the most-watched man on TV act as a cartoony caricature of himself. To this day, Hasselhoff’s appearance in _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_has made him a memorable part of the franchise, to the point where he has cameoed in later _SpongeBob_ projects, including the recent video game _SpongeBob SquarePants: Titans of the Tide._
texts.2:
## Scarlett Johansson - The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie (2004)
Nowadays, most people know who Scarlett Johansson is. Between her tenure in the MCU as Black Widow, her award-winning performances in _Marriage Story_(2019), and her recent box office behemoth _Jurassic World Rebirth_(2025)_,_ she needs no introduction.
Back in 2004, that was hardly the case. While she gained prominence the year before thanks to _Lost In Translation_(2003)_,_ Scarlett Johansson was relatively unknown, especially in the realm of voice acting. Nevertheless, she voiced King Neptune’s daughter, Princess Mindy, in _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie,_ who helped SpongeBob and Patrick on their quest to retrieve her father’s crown. Her cameo is still a surprising reveal to longtime fans, since she was rarely featured in the marketing in the lead-up to the film’s release, and in part because of how she quickly catapulted into the realm of Hollywood A-Lister in the decades that followed. But looking back, this helped introduce her to a mainstream audience and would only be another step in her meteoric rise to stardom.
texts.3:
## Alec Baldwin - The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie (2004)
Rounding out our trio of notable celebrity cameos in _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie_ would be the man who played Dennis, the imposing and dangerous bounty hunter sent to hunt down SpongeBob and Patrick, portrayed by Alec Baldwin.
While Baldwin’s star has dimmed significantly since the release of the film, and mostly in part due to the controversy surrounding the filming of _Rust_(2024), he’s nevertheless a well-known name within the world of cinema. While he’s mostly known for his sardonic wit, seeing him play an intimidating bounty hunter actually manages to work pretty well, channeling a performance that takes some cues from Slade from _Teen Titans_(2003-2007). It’s unexpected to see such an A-list actor play this relatively silent menace, but leave it to Alec Baldwin to get the most out of what should be a simple villain.
texts.4:
## Keanu Reeves - The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run (2020)
For most of the 2010s, Keanu Reeves was seen as the perennial Hollywood badass. Thanks to the popularity of _John Wick_(2014), as well as a breathtaking performance in the video game _Cyberpunk 2077,_ Keanu Reeves was all the rage. So much so that his cameo in _The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run_seemed inevitable.
In it, Keanu Reeves plays a spirit inhabiting a tumbleweed who was meant to guide SpongeBob and Patrick on their journey to rescue Gary. He pops up intermittently to offer courage, positive reinforcement, and the kind of platitudes that you would expect from mentors like Splinter in _Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles_(1987-1996). However, there’s no getting around the fact that just seeing Keanu Reeves’ face inside a tumbleweed is bizarre. Apparently, the role was conceived solely for Reeves, so the uncanny appearance is intentional and part of the joke. It certainly does leave an impact and is probably the most memorable thing about the film, making it just as surprising as Hasselhoff’s role in _The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie._
texts.5:
## Johnny Knoxville - Saving Bikini Bottom: The Sandy Cheeks Movie (2024)
While there have only been four theatrically released _SpongeBob SquarePants_ movies, there have been a few direct-to-streaming feature films that have their own odd and unexpected celebrity cameos. Probably the most unexpected one would have to be Johnny Knoxville appearing as Sandy’s brother Randy in _Saving Bikini Bottom: The Sandy Cheeks Movie_.
While this isn’t Knoxville’s first appearance in the franchise, his role as Randy will definitely be nostalgic to those who remember watching Knoxville on _Jackass_(2000-2001). Randy works at a rodeo and dresses like an Evel Knievel knock-off, and he, alongside the rest of Sandy’s family, helps Sandy and SpongeBob save Bikini Bottom. Even for the little time he’s present in this 82-minute movie, Knoxville shows that he’s grown and matured since his younger days. He’s less obnoxious, and seeing his character lean into what made Knoxville such a fun presence in his early years lets you appreciate Knoxville’s appearance all the more.
texts.6:
## Ice Spice - The SpongeBob Movie: The Search For SquarePants (2025)
It’s not uncommon for animated movies to get a tie-in pop song from a popular artist. Plenty of films have done it, yet seeing Ice Spice not only produce the lead single for _The SpongeBob Movie: The Search For SquarePants_, the infectiously catchy “Big Guy,” and appear as a character is pretty unexpected.
If you’re a fan of her music, though, that shouldn’t be too big of a shock. After all, one of her first singles was titled “Bikini Bottom,” and she talks about how she grew up watching the series. Say what you will about her talent as an artist, but seeing a younger celebrity cameo in a franchise like _SpongeBob SquarePants_ makes perfect sense. Ice Spice herself has also been dipping her toes into acting this year as well, with her recently cameoing in Spike Lee’s _Highest 2 Lowest_ (2025).
Thanks to Nickelodeon’s marketing machine, it’s impossible to separate Ice Spice from _The Search For SquarePants_, and even if she’s only in the movie as much as Johnny Knoxville was in _Saving Bikini Bottom: The Sandy Cheeks Movie,_ that’ll probably be the case for years to come.

Title: Tom Johnson, ‘The Daily Show’ and ‘The Jeselnik Offensive’ Writer, Dies at 55
Chunks: 0,1
Tom Johnson, a writer and stand-up comic with credits including “The Daily Show” and “The Jeselnik Offensive,” has died at the age of 55.
In a statement Friday, his family said he died at his home “Peacefully and unexpectedly” on Jan. 14. No cause of death has been made public.
“Growing up,” the family wrote in their statement, Johnson “had an insatiable curiosity. He was talented in all of the arts: a gifted artist who could draw in vivid detail, played the guitar and trombone, and acted in plays throughout college at the University of Missouri. He loved the band Kiss and enjoyed dressing up like the lead singer for Halloween.”
“Tom had a huge heart and cared deeply about taking care of others. He launched the careers of countless successful comedians. His work ethic was impeccable. He was fair, kind, talented, inclusive, and funny as hell. He was a voracious reader, eater, and rescuer of cats. It brought him great joy to play pranks on those he loved. He will be truly missed by all,” the family statement said also.
Johnson’s death was first revealed on the “WTF with Marc Maron” podcast on Thursday, which he served as executive producer and head writer on in 2010, according to his LinkedIn.
“I knew him back when he did comedy briefly. He was actually at the Comedy Cellar before me and then he became a writer for The Daily Show. This is the pre – Jon Stewart incarnation of ‘The Daily Show’ and that’s sort of how he came to Air America. He started Air America with me but Lizz Winstead, who was at the original ‘Daily Show,’ pulled Tom in as a writer and that’s where we re-met,” Maron said. “He was f—ing hilarious, like inspired as a writer but also as a performer, and he wrote so many amazing bits for us that he did on the radio.”
Johnson began working on the Comedy Central late night program as a writer and performer in May 1996 and worked on the show through January 2004. He wrote on more than 1200 episodes and won two Emmy Awards and two Peabody Awards for his work on the show.

His other credits at the network include co-executive producer and head writer on “Stand Up Nation With Greg Giraldo,” “Adult Content with Greg Giraldo,” and “Reality Bites,”a writer on the roast of David Hasselhoff and head writer on the roast of Roseanne, an executive producer and head writer on “Midnight with Anthony Jeselnik,” co-creator, executive producer and head writer on “The Jeselnik Offensive,” and a writer on “NSFW with Nikki Glaser.”
Outside of Comedy Central, he worked as a head writer and supervising producer on Game Show Network’s “Late Night Liars,” head writer and producer on Fox Broadcasting’s “Talkshow with Spike Feresten,” head writer on Spike TV’s 2010, 2012, 2014, 2015 and 2016 Guys Choice Awards and Scream Awards 2011, the 2016 MTV Music Video Awards, IFC’s Make Me Understand and Zynga’s “Words with Friends Live!,” head writer and producer on TBS’ “Lopez Tonight,” and a writer and supervising producer on MTV’s “Gamekillers.”
Additionally, Johnson served as a writer producer on HBO’s “Savage Love,” a writer on Bravo’s “Straight Talk with Joan Rivers,” A&E Television’s “Balls of Steel,” VH1’s “Best Week Ever,” MTV’s “Race Riot,” Spike TV’s 2009 Video Game Awards, Viacom’s “Martha & Snoop’s Potluck Challenge,”and Quibi’s “Nice One With Ron Funches,” head consultant on the 2014 MTV Music Video Awards, a consultant on Syfy’s “Reactor” and Fox Broadcasting’s “The All-Star Dog Rescue Celebration,” and head consultant, writer and producer on 2020’s NBA All-Star Roast.
Johnson is survived by his wife Rozie Bacchi and his sisters, brothers-in-law, nieces and their families.

Brooks built his entire act around the “lovable drunk” character, slurring his words, wobbling slightly, and delivering insults that sounded half-accidental. But the brilliance was that every pause, stumble, and mispronounced line was perfectly timed. Fellow comedians often struggled to stay in character because they knew he was completely sober while performing the most convincing drunk routine on television. At many roasts, you can see the panel trying not to laugh as Brooks leans into the microphone, loses his train of thought, then suddenly lands a razor-sharp punchline. The contrast between the sloppy delivery and the clever jokes made it unforgettable. Those roast moments became classic TV comedy. ## Career
### Television career
#### _Family Guy_
On July 22, 2007, MacFarlane announced that he might start work on a feature film, although "nothing's official".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-34) In September 2007, Ricky Blitt gave TV.com an interview confirming that he had already started working on the script.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-35) Then in _TV Week_ on July 18, 2008, MacFarlane confirmed plans to produce a theatrically released _Family Guy_ feature film sometime "within the next year".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-36) He came up with an idea for the story, "something that you could not do on the show, which [to him] is the only reason to do a movie".

## Career
### Television career
#### _Family Guy_
He said he imagines the film to be "an old-style musical with dialogue" similar to _The Sound of Music_, saying that he would "really be trying to capture, musically, that feel".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-37) On October 13, 2011, MacFarlane confirmed that a deal for a _Family Guy_ film had been made, and that he would write it with series co-producer Ricky Blitt.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-38) On November 30, 2012, he confirmed plans for the project.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-39) The project was put on hold while MacFarlane worked on _Ted 2_.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-40) In 2018, Fox announced that a live-action/animated film based on the series is in development.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-42) MacFarlane stepped away from the series in 2011 to work on _Ted_ and other projects, and has only worked with the show as a voice actor since.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-43)

## Career
### Television career
#### _Family Guy_
_Family Guy_ has often been criticized.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-44) The Parents Television Council has been a frequent critic. It organized a letter-writing campaign to remove it from Fox's lineup,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-45) and filed complaints with the Federal Communications Commission alleging that some of its episodes contained indecent content.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-46) MacFarlane has responded to the PTC's criticism by saying, among other things: "That's like getting hate mail from Hitler. They're literally terrible human beings."[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-Advocate-47)
_Family Guy_ has been canceled twice, although strong fan support and DVD sales have caused Fox to reconsider.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-48) MacFarlane mentioned how these cancellations affected the lineup of writers: "One of the positive aspects of _Family Guy_ constantly being pulled off [the air] is that we were always having to restaff writers."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-norton-30)
During its sixth season, episodes of _Family Guy_ and _American Dad!_ were delayed from regular broadcast due to the 2007–2008 Writers Guild of America strike. MacFarlane participated in the strike to support the writers, and Fox aired three _Family Guy_ episodes without his permission._[how?_] The strike ended on February 12, 2008.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-cnn1-49)

## Career
### Television career
#### _American Dad!_
MacFarlane has a second long-running adultanimated series in _American Dad!_, which has been in production since early 2005. It is his only animated series that has not been canceled, though it has undergone two network relocations: from Fox to TBS following its 11th season,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-50) and from TBS back to Fox following its 21st.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-51) MacFarlane provides the voices of protagonist Stan Smith and prominent secondary character Roger.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-usatoday-8) His sister Rachael provides the voice of Hayley, Stan's daughter.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-rachael-52) Additionally, he co-wrote the show's first episode.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-Goodman-54) Aside from his voice acting work, MacFarlane has left much of _American Dad!_'s creative direction to the show's other co-creators, Matt Weitzman and Mike Barker (the latter departed after ten seasons),[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-shakeup-56) feeling it helps give the series its own voice and identity.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-doorly1-57)

## Career
### Television career
#### _American Dad!_
MacFarlane has stated that his inspiration to create _American Dad!_ derived from his and Weitzman's exasperation with the George W. Bush administration.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-58) MacFarlane has described the initial seasons of _American Dad!_ as being similar to _All in the Family_, likening Stan's originally bigoted persona to Archie Bunker.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-norton-30) After the early couple of seasons however, the series discontinued using these elements of political satire[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-59) and changed to its own humor.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-doorly1-57) MacFarlane was described as having difficulty understanding the series in its early going; however, he warmed up to the series after its early seasons once he felt the show truly came into its own. His fellow co-creators have sensed this through MacFarlane's greatly increased attention to the series after its early seasons. MacFarlane has revealed he is an _American Dad!_ fan himself. He has taken note of the positive reaction to the Roger character by fans via his Twitter.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-by_Emily_VanDerWerff_September_28,_2012-60)

## Career
### Television career
#### _Family Guy_
On July 22, 2007, MacFarlane announced that he might start work on a feature film, although "nothing's official".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-34) In September 2007, Ricky Blitt gave TV.com an interview confirming that he had already started working on the script.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-35) Then in _TV Week_ on July 18, 2008, MacFarlane confirmed plans to produce a theatrically released _Family Guy_ feature film sometime "within the next year".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-36) He came up with an idea for the story, "something that you could not do on the show, which [to him] is the only reason to do a movie".
texts.13:
## Career
### Television career
#### _Family Guy_
He said he imagines the film to be "an old-style musical with dialogue" similar to _The Sound of Music_, saying that he would "really be trying to capture, musically, that feel".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-37) On October 13, 2011, MacFarlane confirmed that a deal for a _Family Guy_ film had been made, and that he would write it with series co-producer Ricky Blitt.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-38) On November 30, 2012, he confirmed plans for the project.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-39) The project was put on hold while MacFarlane worked on _Ted 2_.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-40) In 2018, Fox announced that a live-action/animated film based on the series is in development.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-42) MacFarlane stepped away from the series in 2011 to work on _Ted_ and other projects, and has only worked with the show as a voice actor since.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-43)
texts.14:
## Career
### Television career
#### _Family Guy_
_Family Guy_ has often been criticized.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-44) The Parents Television Council has been a frequent critic. It organized a letter-writing campaign to remove it from Fox's lineup,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-45) and filed complaints with the Federal Communications Commission alleging that some of its episodes contained indecent content.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-46) MacFarlane has responded to the PTC's criticism by saying, among other things: "That's like getting hate mail from Hitler. They're literally terrible human beings."[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-Advocate-47)
_Family Guy_ has been canceled twice, although strong fan support and DVD sales have caused Fox to reconsider.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-48) MacFarlane mentioned how these cancellations affected the lineup of writers: "One of the positive aspects of _Family Guy_ constantly being pulled off [the air] is that we were always having to restaff writers."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-norton-30)
During its sixth season, episodes of _Family Guy_ and _American Dad!_ were delayed from regular broadcast due to the 2007–2008 Writers Guild of America strike. MacFarlane participated in the strike to support the writers, and Fox aired three _Family Guy_ episodes without his permission._[how?_] The strike ended on February 12, 2008.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-cnn1-49)
texts.15:
## Career
### Television career
#### _American Dad!_
MacFarlane has a second long-running adultanimated series in _American Dad!_, which has been in production since early 2005. It is his only animated series that has not been canceled, though it has undergone two network relocations: from Fox to TBS following its 11th season,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-50) and from TBS back to Fox following its 21st.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-51) MacFarlane provides the voices of protagonist Stan Smith and prominent secondary character Roger.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-usatoday-8) His sister Rachael provides the voice of Hayley, Stan's daughter.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-rachael-52) Additionally, he co-wrote the show's first episode.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-Goodman-54) Aside from his voice acting work, MacFarlane has left much of _American Dad!_'s creative direction to the show's other co-creators, Matt Weitzman and Mike Barker (the latter departed after ten seasons),[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-shakeup-56) feeling it helps give the series its own voice and identity.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-doorly1-57)
texts.16:
## Career
### Television career
#### _American Dad!_
MacFarlane has stated that his inspiration to create _American Dad!_ derived from his and Weitzman's exasperation with the George W. Bush administration.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-58) MacFarlane has described the initial seasons of _American Dad!_ as being similar to _All in the Family_, likening Stan's originally bigoted persona to Archie Bunker.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-norton-30) After the early couple of seasons however, the series discontinued using these elements of political satire[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-59) and changed to its own humor.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-doorly1-57) MacFarlane was described as having difficulty understanding the series in its early going; however, he warmed up to the series after its early seasons once he felt the show truly came into its own. His fellow co-creators have sensed this through MacFarlane's greatly increased attention to the series after its early seasons. MacFarlane has revealed he is an _American Dad!_ fan himself. He has taken note of the positive reaction to the Roger character by fans via his Twitter.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_MacFarlane#cite_note-by_Emily_VanDerWerff_September_28,_2012-60)
